rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=100, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-8 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: per-scene steps n_iter 30->100, on the iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 SSIM0.9606 PSNR39.57 (img_sr 0.0005->0.0002 marginal +0.0004 over iter-5's 0.1257; range-sigma optimum is flat ~2e-4..5e-4). HYPOTHESIS: iter-1/iter-3 showed n_iter did NOT help when img_sr was WIDE (0.02) -- more steps just pulled the over-smoothing BF further toward the blurry 64-view half-target. But now img_sr is TIGHT/edge-preserving, so additional per-scene N2I steps should refine the edge-preserving denoiser toward better noise suppression WITHOUT over-blurring (the tight range kernel structurally cannot cross edges regardless of step count) -> hr climbs above 0.1261. If hr FLAT/DROPS, the edge-preserving BF converges fast (30 steps already enough) and n_iter is saturated -> revert to 30 and move to spatial sigma. FAILURE watched: even edge-preserving, too many steps could still creep the recon toward the noisy half-target mean (mild PSNR drop). BUDGET: n_iter 30->100 ~3.3x inner steps; iter-7 ran 692s at n_iter30 on a fast node but iter-1 n_iter120 was 1200s -> n_iter100 ~1000-1100s; outer_wall_s=900 caps it (may trim a few scenes). ONE knob: n_iter 30->100.
